ideas: The situation and why you had little time
The options you had and what you chose
Whether it was the right call

phrases.meaning: something bad that turns out good

model: I want to talk about a quick decision I made last year when I was travelling to Da Nang for a friend's wedding. I was sitting at the airport in Hanoi, and I was scrolling through my phone when an announcement said my flight was delayed by five hours. That meant I'd miss the rehearsal dinner, which I'd promised to help with. So I had to decide on the spot. First, I tried to weigh up the options. I could wait for the flight, or I could buy a ticket with a different airline that was leaving in forty minutes, but it cost almost twice as much. There wasn't really time to think it through, so I just went with my gut and bought the new ticket. Then I ran to the other check-in desk, and while I was queueing, I was texting my friend to say I might still make it. After that, it was a bit of a rush through security, but I got on the plane just before the gate closed. In the end, it was definitely the right call. I arrived in time, helped set up the tables, and my friend was really grateful. I think it taught me that I can think on my feet when I'm under pressure. It was expensive, but for me it was worth every dong.
